context.title: Arrested, Denied, Tried
context.summary: Jesus is arrested in a garden across the Kidron; Peter cuts off a servant's ear. Annas questions Jesus while Peter denies him. Before Pilate, Jesus says his kingdom is not of this world, and the crowd chooses Barabbas.
context.background: Annas had been high priest from AD 6 to 15 and remained powerful; Josephus says five of his sons became high priest, and his son-in-law Caiaphas held the office then. Roman law kept the power of execution from the Jewish council (v. 31).

customs.note: Entering a Gentile's residence was thought to make a Jew ritually unclean, which would bar them from eating the Passover.

watchFor: When Jesus says 'I am he', the soldiers fall back (v. 6).
Peter warms himself at a 'fire of coals' (v. 18), a detail that returns in chapter 21.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Judas
people.summary: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Malchus
people.summary: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10).

people.name: Caiaphas
people.summary: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius (Luke 3:2), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion (Matt. 26:3, 57; John 11:49; 18:13, 14).

people.name: Annas
people.summary: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2).

people.name: Pontius
people.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

people.name: Barabbas
people.summary: I.e., son of Abba or of a father, a notorious robber whom Pilate proposed to condemn to death instead of Jesus, whom he wished to release, in accordance with the Roman custom (John 18:40; Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19).

places.name: brook Kidron
places.summary: The black torrent, the brook flowing through the ravine below the eastern wall of Jerusalem (John 18:1).

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

events.title: Holy Week
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 21:1 – John 20:31. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 8 days.

events.title: Prayer and Betrayal in Gethsemane
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 26:36 – John 18:12. People: Jesus, Judas, Simon. Place: Gethsemane.

events.title: Jewish Trials
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 26:57 – John 18:27. People: Jesus, Simon, Caiaphas. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Roman Trials
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 27:11 – John 19:16. People: Jesus, Simon, Pontius, Barabbas. Place: Jerusalem.
